faqs.question: What does ADA Test - Synovial Fluid measure?
faqs.answer: ADA Test - Synovial Fluid measures the levels of adenosine deaminase (ADA) enzyme activity in the synovial fluid.

faqs.question: Why is ADA Test - Synovial Fluid done?
faqs.answer: • To rule out tuberculosis and other inflammatory conditions affecting the joints • To aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, septic arthritis, and reactive arthritis • To assess the effectiveness of treatment for tuberculosis or other inflammatory diseases involving the joints

faqs.question: When is ADA Test - Synovial Fluid recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if • you have symptoms such as joint pain, swelling, stiffness, or limited mobility, • your doctor suspects tuberculosis or other inflammatory conditions affecting the joints, or • you have been diagnosed with a condition that requires monitoring of joint inflammation.

faqs.question: What if the results of the ADA Test - Synovial Fluid are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Elevated levels may indicate tuberculosis or other inflammatory conditions.

faqs.question: What to expect during the ADA Test - Synovial Fluid?
faqs.answer: During the test, a small amount of synovial fluid will be collected from your joint using a sterile needle and syringe. The collected synovial fluid will be sent to the laboratory for analysis by biochemical method.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the ADA Test - Synovial Fluid?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, as certain medications may interfere with the test results. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any specific instructions provided by your doctor regarding fasting or discontinuing certain medications.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with ADA Test - Synovial Fluid?
faqs.answer: • Joint fluid analysis: Examination of synovial fluid for various components to aid in the diagnosis of joint-related conditions. • Tuberculosis tests: Tests such as a chest x-ray, sputum culture, or interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) help to confirm or rule out tuberculosis infection.

faqs.question: What is the ADA Test - Synovial Fluid also known as?
faqs.answer: Synovial Fluid ADA Test or ADA Enzyme Assay

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also involve other organs, including the joints. Symptoms include cough, weight loss, fever, night sweats, and fatigue.
